title: Dabur India Faces SEBI Warning for Delay in Reporting USFDA Regulatory Letter
summary: New Delhi: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has issued an administrative warning to Dabur India Limited for delaying the disclosure of a warning letter received from the United States...

contentHtml:
New Delhi: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has issued an administrative warning to Dabur India Limited for delaying the disclosure of a warning letter received from the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) on July 24, 2026, alleging non-compliance with disclosure requirements under the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

In an administrative warning letter dated November 6, 2026, SEBI stated that its examination of Dabur India revealed a violation of Regulation 30(6)(iii) of the SEBI Listing Regulations due to the delay in disclosing the USFDA warning letter. The warning was issued under Regulation 30 read with Sub-para 20 of Para A of Part A of Schedule III of the SEBI Listing Regulations.

The communication was issued by SEBI's Corporation Finance Department, Division of Supervision, Enforcement and Complaints – 5, and addressed to Dabur India Limited at its registered office in New Delhi. The letter was addressed to Ashok Kumar Jain, Group Company Secretary and Chief Compliance Officer of the company.

SEBI stated that the alleged non-compliance had been viewed seriously and warned the company and its Board of Directors to exercise caution in the future to prevent the recurrence of such lapses. The regulator further cautioned that any repetition of the violation would be viewed seriously and could invite appropriate enforcement action under the SEBI Act, 1992, and the rules, regulations or circulars issued thereunder.

The regulator also directed Dabur India to place the administrative warning communication before its Board of Directors at the upcoming board meeting. The company was asked to forward the Board's comments to SEBI regarding whether it was satisfied with the corrective measures taken to ensure compliance with disclosure requirements in the future.

Additionally, SEBI advised the company to disclose the administrative warning letter to the stock exchanges under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015.

Dabur India informed the stock exchanges about the receipt of the administrative warning through a regulatory filing dated November 6, 2026, submitted to BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE).

According to the company's regulatory disclosure, SEBI had issued an administrative warning and advisory letter asking Dabur India to exercise caution in the future to avoid similar lapses, particularly delays in making regulatory disclosures.

Dabur India stated that the warning letter alleged a violation of Regulation 30(6)(iii) of the SEBI Listing Regulations on account of the delayed disclosure of the USFDA warning letter received on July 24, 2026. The company also clarified that the administrative warning issued by SEBI would have no impact on its financial operations or other business activities.

In its communication to the exchanges, Dabur India stated that it had always been among the most compliant companies in following SEBI Listing Regulations and that it would take the necessary steps to address the concerns and directives mentioned in the warning letter.

Dabur India Limited is headquartered in New Delhi and operates across the healthcare, personal care and consumer goods sectors.
